content_html:
Probabilistic Memory

Select – Change – Reconstruct

Memory is not perfect playback but a probabilistic reconstruction of distributed neural patterns. At every stage—selection of inputs, synaptic change, and recall—the system represents and resolves uncertainty. This aligns naturally with our cycle: Select → Change → Reconstruct.

Neural noise is functional: variable synaptic release and population codes support inference under uncertainty.
Memory is reconstructive: recall completes patterns from partial cues, guided by priors and schemas.
Decision signals are stochastic: diffusion-like accumulation in parietal cortex explains variable choices & times.

Mechanisms

Stage Probabilistic Mechanisms Implications
Select Likelihood-based sensory codes; attention weighted by priors and goals; predictive coding minimizes prediction error. Only probable, relevant signals are strongly encoded; ambiguous inputs are resolved using prior knowledge.
Change Synaptic vesicle
release probability
(Pr) varies by bouton; plasticity rules are stochastic; each reactivation induces slight drift.		 Traces adapt and generalize (preventing overfitting) but can deviate from original details.
Reconstruct Hippocampal CA3 performs pattern completion; recall approximates Bayesian inference over cues + priors; decisions exhibit diffusion-like stochasticity. Recall is flexible and efficient under uncertainty but susceptible to distortion and false memories.

Note on frameworks: Bayesian/predictive coding accounts offer a powerful description of probabilistic inference in the brain; ongoing debates highlight where these are metaphors vs. mechanistic implementations.
